evidence: Judge agent+model pinned once, in the shared block: task.toml:30-35 [verifier.env] REWARDKIT_JUDGE="claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api", ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" - exactly the frozen block in staged-task-contract.md. All five judge.toml [judge] blocks carry only judge="claude-code" (expected fallback), mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template; grep for model|temperature|reasoning across tests/*/*/judge.toml returns nothing. test.sh:63-66 refuses to grade (zero reward) if REWARDKIT_JUDGE/MODEL are unset, so no silent default model. Pinned CLIs and browser: tests/Dockerfile:16-22 npm -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1; :31 harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7; :33-38 Chromium installed by the playwright CLI bundled inside the pinned @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and symlinked to /usr/local/bin/chromium; every judge.toml launches playwright-mcp with --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium --headless --isolated. Shared tools pinned: tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/tools/score.py, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/scoring.toml, tests/.dockerignore and environment/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty; score.py 13de2b38..., restart_mcp.py 03c1426f... equal in both). Fixed clock: no graded rule depends on the calendar date or run date. hireops_rules.md has no aging/expiry/'today'/business-day rules; unread and seen are defined by read-count markers and message order (hireops_rules.md section 6, section 9 'how many messages ... counted from its first'), not timestamps. Grep of every judge.toml/prompt.md for clock|today|date|timestamp|ago|minutes|hours|days finds only 'out-of-date' (version conflict, judge.toml:200 / functional prompt.md:33) and elapsed-time '15 seconds' live-update windows (judge.toml:290,299,344,353; functional prompt.md:47 instructs 'accept what is present at the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds'), which are real-time latency bounds, not calendar rules, and are stated publicly (instruction.md:5, hireops_rules.md section 5). Seed timestamps are fixed literals (2026-07-14..2026-07-29Z); the golden orders messages, activity and notes by autoincrement id (index.js:158,189,378,395,399-400), so wall-clock now() (index.js:59) only stamps new rows and never changes a graded outcome; display uses fixed UTC (app.js:21). Because no time rule is graded, the contract's 'fixed clock' cross-file row is vacuous here and its absence from instruction.md is not a defect for this row. Network: task.toml:22,38 public - correct per delivery profile, not reported. Raw evidence index hashes (workspace.cjs 749036d0..., workspace.json 1c7e6fcc..., server.log 6752f461..., three PNGs) and the matching source hashes (index.js b07109f8..., db.js 0367a73b..., seed a1c65c80..., solve.sh 1df2ed04...) re-verified equal to current bytes; that evidence is a scripted golden run, not a configured judge run, and is not needed to establish static pinning. Adversarial probes: (a) broken app that could pass because of nondeterminism - none found tied to pinning; LLM judge sampling variance is inherent and the workbook explicitly does not require temperature. (b) conforming alternative that could fail because of the clock - an app sorting messages by created_at with wall-clock stamps still places new messages after the July-2026 seed on any realistic run date, and relative 'x days ago' labels are not graded; no counterexample found.
notes: Non-blocking, template-controlled observations (do not edit shared harness): base images node:22-bookworm-slim and python:3.12-slim are tag-pinned not digest-pinned, apt packages unpinned (check-dockerfiles.py treats unpinned apt as NOTE), and the Chromium build is pinned transitively through @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 rather than by an explicit version string. Internal sheet row 47 still mentions temperature 0 / versioned prompt; the client sheet and skill reference supersede it. No full configured judge run exists, so run-to-run judge variance is unmeasured; that is a workload/discrimination evidence gap owned by other rows, not a pinning defect.
